newsitem.title: USA: Amoco to build Miss. gas plant with Shell.
newsitem.headline: Amoco to build Miss. gas plant with Shell.

text.p: Amoco Corp said Wednesday it plans to build a cryogenic natural gas processing plant near Pascagoula, Miss., with Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
The cost of the proposed project was not disclosed.
Amoco said it will own 60 percent, and Shell 40 percent, of the plant, which will have processing capacity of one billion cubic feet of gas per day.
The plant will be connected to the Destin Pipeline, an offshore pipeline to be jointly owned by Amoco, Shell and Sonat Inc, the energy giant said.
"This is a major milestone for the industry," said Wayne Heth, vice president of Chicago-based Amoco's natural gas liquids business unit.
"This signals a major new transportation and processing system to accommodate the significant new natural gas resources discovered in the eastern portion of the deepwater Gulf of Mexico," he said.
Bechtel Corp will design and build the plant, with construction expected to begin in the fourth quarter, Amoco said.
